declaration.authority_note: P6.8: this object is the ONE runtime service-level declaration. Nothing else in the repository may declare an end-to-end runtime objective. The two declarations it replaces are recorded in `supersedes` with the reason each was wrong; scripts/lib/runtime_slo.mjs refuses this asset if either reappears, and refuses it if the numbers below stop agreeing with the constants the runtime actually enforces.

supersedes.why_wrong: UNSATISFIABLE, not merely different. 35 minutes (2100000 ms) and 45 minutes (2700000 ms) both exceed the enforced end_to_end_hard_ceiling of 1500000 ms, so a run that met this 'objective' would already have exhausted the only clock it has. It had zero code consumers until P6.6 read the trace bands beside it, and assets/deployment-profile.json still describes this file as the canonical v3.6 timing policy: it is stale v3.6 text, not a live objective.

It restates the hard ceiling as an objective. A ceiling is the line at which a run is refused more budget; declaring it as the p95 of a SUBSET path asserts that 5% of the cheapest path may run to the absolute maximum, and makes a subset path slower than the whole-run p95. The no-broker path is governed by the single end_to_end objective below.

end_to_end_ms.p50_note: Equal to DEFAULT_RUNTIME_BUDGETS_MS.end_to_end_target, which the instruction surfaces state as 'the ordinary end-to-end target is fifteen minutes'. An ordinary run is the median run, so the enforced target IS the p50; the budget policy has no percentile vocabulary of its own.
end_to_end_ms.p95_note: Twenty minutes. This is the only band the enforcement layer never had: it sits strictly between the target and the ceiling, so a tail run may exceed the ordinary target without being at the point of refusal.
end_to_end_ms.hard_ceiling_note: Equal to DEFAULT_RUNTIME_BUDGETS_MS.end_to_end_hard_ceiling and to the instruction surfaces' twenty-five-minute hard ceiling.

enforced_envelope.note: P6.1 bounded the stage floor instead of removing it, so the ceiling is enforced as an ENVELOPE: a run may be granted at most the ceiling plus a finite, ledger-recorded floor allowance, after which every further grant collapses to 1 ms. Declaring the envelope here keeps it from becoming a fourth, hidden declaration.
enforced_envelope.in_process_preemption_note: Grants are enforced by construction at every consult and by subprocess timeout at the one spawn boundary. A stage running inside the controller process is charged and typed on overrun (INTERNAL.runtime_budget_overrun) but is not preempted, so overshoot must be DISCLOSED by a receipt rather than assumed impossible.

cohort.measurement_source_note: A sample is admissible only if it carries the run's own persisted run-deadline.json reading: the run id, the ledger digest, and a compute_elapsed_ms that reconciles against the ledger's labelled segments. A hand-supplied duration is not a measurement.
cohort.warm_p95_note: P6.3/P6.4 made reuse real and enacted. Reuse that makes a run slower is a defect, so the warm cohort's p95 is compared against the cold cohort's.

component_objectives_ms.note: Sub-path objectives, each of which must be no greater than the end-to-end p95 and no greater than the sum of the stage budgets that bound it.

scopes.end_to_end_delivery: Every user stage from inputs through delivery, ending in a delivered workbook. The only scope that can CERTIFY the end-to-end objective.
scopes.evidence_half_through_decisions: Stages inputs, evidence_review and decisions, ending in the lawful PAUSED boundary. A strict subset, so its percentiles bound the end-to-end objective from BELOW and can refute it but never certify it.
